features.title: Split Order

split.description: Split Order (DRAFT, not in spec): allow a large single job to be split across multiple vehicles when no single vehicle has enough capacity. Jobs only (not shipments).

can_be_split.description: Whether this job may be split. Default false.

max_splits.description: Maximum number of splits for this job.

quant.description: Minimum quantity of each split as a ratio of job load. Applies only when the problem load dimension is 1 (multi-dimension behavior is TBC per the doc).

rules: split applies to single jobs only; shipments are not supported.
The sub-jobs created by a split share the SAME job id as the original.
If a job's demand exceeds capacity and can_be_split is false or absent -> the job is UNASSIGNED (HTTP 200, result.code 0, job in result.unassigned).
If can_be_split is true and there are enough vehicles -> the job is split across vehicles; each split's pickup/delivery sub-volume sums to the original job's value.
Response (informational, not request-validated): route steps carry split_indicator (int, 0-based, strictly less than max_splits) and per-split pickup/delivery arrays.
testingSuggestions: High delivery volume (e.g. ~5x a single vehicle's capacity) with can_be_split=false or absent -> expect the job in result.unassigned.
Same high-volume job with can_be_split=true, max_splits sufficient, and ~5 vehicles -> expect a valid solution where the job is split across vehicles (sub-deliveries sum to the original).
Malformed split input (e.g. wrong types, or split on a shipment) -> expect HTTP 400 input validation failed.
Boundary: max_splits exactly equal to the number of vehicles needed; quant at the minimum ratio.
limitations: quant multi-dimension load behavior is undefined in the source doc (mark TBC).
